column1: # TITLE: Endothelial stromal cells enhance lung-tumor cell migration through TNFα and SDF-1α secretion
# SUMMARY: Recent studies have noted the tumor-stroma interaction as an integral part of tumor growth and spread as well as novel avenues for effective treatment. However
column2: the details by which tumor and stroma cells communicate remain poorly understood. Here we show that the migration speed of the non-small-cell lung tumor cell line H838 is significantly increased under the influence of human pulmonary endothelial cells
column4: in a transfilter co-culture system. To elucidate the effect of cell communication on the increased tumor cell migration
column5: we record the H838 transcriptome response after the induction of migration in a hetero- and homogenous co-culture conditions. Gene Set enrichment analysis indicates a migration response of H838 in heterogenous co-culture system. Moreover
column6: computationally transcription factor analysis relates the specific gene expression response to the cytokine-induced up-stream receptor activity and subsequently linking these factors to the upstream receptors via shortest paths across a directed protein-protein interaction network. This analysis predicted TNF- and SDF-1 signaling as well as multiple receptors upstream of Stat3 as putative mediators of the transcriptome response. To close the signaling information path from transcription factors to the possible receptor activation
column7: we determine secretome quantification using a cytokine array. The latter revealed the predicted TNFa
column8: SDF-1a signaling molecules as well as other known migration cytokines
column10: as possible candidates for increased migration. Addition through the recombinant proteins or respected inhibitions reveal TNFa as well as SDF-1a as an immediate and early-late secreted factors that cause the increase in H838 migration. Interestingly
column11: both factors were not regulated on the gene level of the H838 in heterogenous co-culture conditions
column12: consequential HPAEC produce TNFa and SDF1a as shown by qPCR technique. Concluding
column13: our combined computational and experimental approach revealed a holistic overview on the migration enhancement of lung tumor cells due to endothelial derived factors. Increase in migration is caused by an early TNFa induced inflammation response followed by a SDF-1a activity to sustaining the phenotype of migration. This tumor-endothelial-communication give a new insight for tumor migration.
